meta_description: Blockchain analytics mapped to regulatory duties: precision-first transaction screening, travel-rule integration and an examination pack prepared before the examiner asks.

blocks.x: Ledger intelligence mapped to regulatory duties: transaction risk scoring with measured precision, travel-rule workflows that cover your counterparties, and case management that turns investigations from archaeology into a query, built for the auditor who arrives unannounced.
Screening precision is a compliance outcome — not a vendor spec sheet
blocks.sub: Attribution discipline and reason-coded alerts that analysts and examiners trust

blocks.x: When value moves on ledgers, compliance duties follow: sanctions screening, travel-rule information transfer, AML case management. The practice builds the intelligence layer, address clustering, risk scoring on flows, and case files that assemble themselves from ledger evidence instead of analyst archaeology.

The design principle: every regulatory duty maps to a pipeline stage with evidence. A case file that a regulator can read, transaction graph, screening results, decisions, timestamps, is the deliverable, not a dashboard.
Below: the failure modes that flood compliance teams with noise, the reference architecture of the analytics pipeline, and the console that keeps case SLAs honest.
Noise to blind spots: how screening fails compliance teams
blocks.sub: Recall theater, uncited attribution, stale models, screenshot evidence

blocks.x: Every one of these converts a regulator's question into a week of work, the countermeasures measure precision, close travel-rule gaps and keep cases queryable from day one.

Precision is the compliance outcome
blocks.sub: Clustering discipline, reason-coded alerts and case assembly that regulators can read

blocks.x: Analytics programs drown compliance teams by optimizing recall: every address looks suspicious, every alert lacks context, and analysts stop trusting the queue. The discipline runs the other way, attribution sources are ranked and cited, clustering heuristics carry confidence bands, and every alert ships with reason codes tied to the specific risk rule that fired. Precision becomes the headline metric because a screened-and-cleared population that survives regulatory sampling is worth more than a noisy one; the console reports precision, coverage and the alert-to-case conversion funnel as standing numbers.

Case assembly is where the audit survives: flagged flows assemble into evidence packs with the transaction graph, the attribution basis, the screening history and the analyst's disposition, exported in the format an examiner expects, not a screenshot bundle. Model changes run through validation with population-drift monitors on both the attribution layer and the risk scores, because sanctions lists and mixing patterns move monthly, and a stale model is a silent compliance debt.

items: The rule, the confidence and the attribution basis ride the alert.

How do you reduce false positives without missing real risk?

Precision is measured per flow class against signed alert budgets, with coverage reported alongside, the examinable claim is the pair, never precision alone. Attribution quality is tuned on your transaction mix, not a vendor demo set.
Yes, travel-rule messaging integrates with the case systems, and the overlay maps each duty (VASP due diligence, sanctions screening, reporting) to the artifact it produces for the examination file.
Can you work with our existing screening vendor?

Where the incumbent holds on measured precision, we keep it. Attribution quality is measured against your flows cycle by cycle, and the defaults table names exactly when a vendor deviation is worth signing.
What does an examiner actually get?

The examination overlay produces the pack: model documentation, precision and coverage evidence per cycle, case outcomes and the reconciliation of alerts to reports, prepared in advance, not reconstructed under deadline.
How quickly do new typologies get into screening?
Typology updates are release-gated: a new pattern enters with its precision evidence on historical data, then shadow-runs before live alerting. The gates table names the evidence each step demands.

blocks.x: Ask what percentage of last month's screening hits your team closed as actionable. The diagnostic will calibrate precision against your closed cases, and price what a quieter, defensible compliance stack costs.
